what: Fulton Financial is a regional bank based in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, serving consumers and businesses in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware and Virginia with loans, deposits and wealth management.
customers: Households and small and mid-sized businesses in the Mid-Atlantic.
money: Commercial real estate and business loans
Home mortgages, home equity and consumer loans
Investment advice, trust and banking fees
moat: Long-standing local relationships and a deposit base built over more than a century.
risks: Lower interest rates can reduce lending margins
opportunities: Net income rose to $403 million over the last twelve months from $289 million in 2024
P/E of about 11 and a dividend yield of about 3.3%
Branches and deposits added through the 2024 Republic First deal
watch: Net interest margin, deposit costs and credit quality in commercial real estate.
view: Fulton is a classic Mid-Atlantic regional bank, and its numbers have improved. Net income rose from about $289 million in 2024 to $403 million over the last twelve months, helped by the deposits and branches it took over from Republic First in 2024.

The valuation is modest: about 11 times trailing earnings and 10 times next year’s estimate, with a dividend yield of about 3.3%. That pricing reflects how investors view regional banks generally after 2023, rather than anything specific to Fulton.

The risks are the usual ones for a bank of this size: commercial real estate loans, competition for deposits and the direction of interest rates. Analysts expect only about 5% EPS growth next year, so the case rests on steady earnings and dividends rather than rapid growth.
bull: Credit stays clean, margins hold and the stock trades closer to book value as sentiment on regional banks improves.
bear: Commercial real estate losses rise or lower rates squeeze margins.
